title: LETTER 8: Letter to Finance Minister — Suggestion on Agricultural Credit

blocks.content: Topic: Write a letter to the Union Finance Minister suggesting ways to improve the flow of formal credit to small and marginal farmers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Formal letters to ministers should maintain an objective, respectful tone supported by structured policy proposals.
Suggestions should focus on strengthening institutional credit through NABARD, RRBs, and Commercial Banks.
Key reform areas include raising collateral-free loan limits, enhancing the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme, and strengthening interest subvention.
A well-structured formal letter contains a concise subject, clear problem statement, specific recommendations, and a polite closing.

blocks.content: Ensuring timely and affordable agricultural credit to small and marginal farmers is essential for sustaining rural growth and ensuring national food security.
Subject: Strengthening Formal Agricultural Credit for Small and Marginal Farmers

I take the liberty of writing to you as a banking professional deeply engaged with agricultural lending. While India has achieved remarkable progress in agricultural credit disbursement — the flow of agricultural credit crossed Rs. 20 lakh crore in 2023-24 — the reality on the ground reveals a persistent and troubling gap: small and marginal farmers (those with landholding below 2 hectares), who constitute nearly 86% of all farm households, continue to rely heavily on informal moneylenders for their credit needs.

The reasons are well-documented: complex documentation requirements, inadequate awareness of schemes like the Kisan Credit Card (KCC), the physical distance of bank branches from remote villages, and the reluctance of banks to lend to tenant farmers who lack formal land titles. Consequently, millions of farmers pay 24–60% annual interest to private lenders instead of accessing bank credit at the effective rate of 4% under the KCC interest subvention scheme.

I respectfully suggest the following policy interventions: (i) mandate all banks to link every PM-KISAN beneficiary to a KCC account within six months; (ii) simplify the KCC documentation for loans up to Rs. 1.6 lakh to just Aadhaar, land record or tenancy agreement, and self-declaration; (iii) expand the CGTMSE guarantee cover to agricultural loans up to Rs. 3 lakh — removing the need for land mortgage for small borrowers; (iv) increase the number of Business Correspondents (BCs) with specific mandate for agricultural outreach in each gram panchayat; and (v) create a centralised digital land records system accessible to banks across all states to eliminate the delay caused by paper-based land verification.
I am confident that these measures, implemented with urgency, will channelise formal credit to India's most deserving and vulnerable farming households.

items: Ensure strict adherence to formal letter formatting: Sender's Address, Date, Receiver's Address, Subject, Salutation, Body, and Sign-off.
Incorporate relevant banking and agricultural terminology like KCC, Priority Sector Lending (PSL), and Interest Subvention Scheme for higher marks.
Keep recommendations realistic and policy-aligned to demonstrate analytical depth in SBI PO, RBI Grade B, and NABARD descriptive tests.

blocks.content: A Concerned Banking and Agricultural Finance Professional

Examiner's Tip: Policy suggestion letters to senior officials must demonstrate data literacy (86% small/marginal farmers, 20 lakh crore credit flow) and specific, numbered recommendations. Each suggestion should be concrete and implementable — not vague.
